title: Lay three bacon rashers flat on a sheet pan with tongs, side by side, none folded or overlapping
instruction: Lay the bacon out on the sheet pan for the oven, using the tongs.
context: Laying bacon strips in a single layer on a sheet pan is a recognizable home-cooking task when preparing bacon in the oven. Folded or overlapping strips cook unevenly. The physical challenge is handling a limp strip through spring tongs: touch its free end down, then trail the rest out flat without folding it or covering a neighbouring strip. Dry silicone strips preserve the handling challenge while keeping the shared rig free of food and grease.
setup: Bench, robot side at the front. (1) Quarter sheet pan, bare aluminium, 23 x 33 cm outside, 2.5 cm rim, flat floor 20 x 30 cm (e.g. Nordic Ware Naturals Quarter Sheet), long side left-right, its centre 31.5 cm ahead of the line through the arm bases and 5 cm left of the centre line. (2) Deli tray, rigid black plastic, 16 x 23 cm outside (15 x 22 cm inside), 2.5 cm deep, long side left-right, butted 2 mm from the pan's right-hand short side and centred on it front-to-back. Pan and tray are taped to the bench. (3) Three bacon stand-ins: 250 x 35 mm strips cut from 1/8 in (3.2 mm) 40A food-grade silicone rubber sheet (e.g. USA Industrials BULK-RS-S40CLRFDA-10, 12 x 12 in; about 30 g per strip; 3 mm in the simulator), dry. They lie lengthwise in the tray, shingled: each strip 22 mm further from the robot than the one under it (centres 29.3, 31.5 and 33.7 cm ahead of the base line, the farthest on top), left ends resting across the tray rim and the pan rim and sticking 20 mm out over the pan floor. (4) Spring tongs, stainless, 24 cm, flat 16 mm ends, no lock, opening about 6 cm at the tips, about 90 g (e.g. Winco UT-9), lying one arm above the other on a stand behind the pan: hinge 47.5 cm ahead of the base line and 25 cm left of the centre line, tips pointing right. (5) Tongs stand: two 75 mm tall posts (22 x 12 mm, 185 mm apart, 8 mm side lips) on a 60 x 250 mm base; the lower arm lies across the posts, 7.5 cm above the bench. Nothing else is on the bench.
scoring: A rasher counts as laid when, at the end, all of it is on the pan's 20 x 30 cm flat floor, no point of it is more than 5 mm above the floor (a folded or stacked part is at least 6 mm), its two ends are at least 235 mm apart (of 250), and seen from above it does not cover any part of another rasher (edges may touch). It counts only if it was carried in the tongs (both jaws on it while it was at least 6 cm up) and no gripper ever came within 10 mm of it; both are latched for the episode. Score: 0.25 per laid rasher (0.25, 0.5, 0.75); 1.0 when all three are laid, the tongs are back on their stand within 3 cm of where they started, both gripper centre points are at least 4 cm from the tongs and every rasher, and everything has been still for 1 s. Otherwise the score is the count at the end of the run. Real trial: one photo from directly above with a ruler in view gives floor containment, end-to-end length and overlap; height is checked by passing a 5 mm gauge (a 5 mm hex key lying on the pan floor under a straightedge) over each strip; tongs use is read from the two camera videos, and any visible gripper contact with a strip in either video voids that strip; a strip that ends off the pan is not laid; the stand has an outline marked for the 3 cm check.
reset_notes: Put the three strips back in the tray in the shingled layout (a paper template under the tray marks the three centre lines and the 20 mm overhang line), and the tongs back on the stand, tips right. Nothing is consumed; a 12 x 12 in sheet yields eight strips, so keep spares and replace any strip that is nicked or torn. Once per silicone sheet, check the stand-in (2 minutes): (a) droop: lay a strip on a table with 83 mm over the edge, held down by a book at the edge; its free end must hang 30 to 50 mm below the table top (simulator: 45 mm); (b) friction: lay a strip on the bare pan and tilt the pan; it must not slide below 30 degrees (simulator friction 0.9 static, 0.8 sliding). If it slides sooner, wash strip and pan with dish soap and dry them. The grippers touch only the dry stainless tongs; no food, grease or liquid is used.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Each rasher is six rigid 42 x 35 x 3 mm links on five sprung hinges, so it bends only across its width. Hinge stiffness and friction (0.9) are calculated from the named sheet's data, not measured; the demo also scores 1.0 at friction 0.6, 1.0 and 1.3. Dry silicone stands in for bacon: no stickiness or grease. Rashers start separated and shingled, so parting a slab is not tested. Pan, tray and stand are fixed; nothing about the rashers is scripted.
